# Spring Break Family Road Trip: San Antonio → Austin → Houston

## 1. Rental Car

**Recommendation: Mid-size SUV** (e.g., Toyota RAV4, Ford Escape)
- Room for 4 people + luggage, comfortable for highway driving
- Estimated cost: **$350–$500** for 7–8 days with a one-way drop-off fee

**Tips for best deals:**
- Book through **Costco Travel** or **AutoSlash** — both consistently beat direct booking rates
- One-way drop-offs between SAT and HOU are common and often have minimal or no extra fee (both are major Texas airports)
- Pick up/drop off at the airport; off-airport locations are cheaper but not worth the hassle with kids and luggage
- Book now but check again 2 weeks before — rates fluctuate and most reservations are fully cancellable
- Decline the rental company's insurance if your personal auto policy or credit card already covers rentals (call and verify before the trip)
- **Drop off at HOU (Hobby)** rather than IAH since your flight departs from Hobby — shorter logistics on departure morning

**Pickup:** SAT airport, April 10 afternoon
**Drop-off:** HOU Hobby, April 17 evening or April 18 early morning (depends on whether you stay overnight in Houston)

---

## 2. Hotels

### San Antonio (3 Nights: April 10–13)

| Hotel | Price/Night (approx.) | Pros | Cons | Why It's Good for Families |
|-------|----------------------|------|------|---------------------------|
| **Drury Inn & Suites Riverwalk** | $160–$200 | Free hot breakfast, free evening "kickback" (drinks + snacks), pool, steps from Riverwalk | Rooms are modest in size | Free breakfast and evening food saves ~$50/day for a family of 4; indoor/outdoor pool keeps kids happy after long days |
| **Holiday Inn San Antonio Riverwalk** | $140–$180 | Rooftop pool with river views, great location, kids eat free program | Older property, rooms are dated | Rooftop pool is a huge hit with kids; kids-eat-free policy is a real budget saver; central Riverwalk location |
| **Hyatt Place San Antonio Riverwalk** | $170–$220 | Modern rooms, free breakfast, pull-out sofas, pool | Slightly pricier | Spacious rooms with separate sleeping areas; modern and clean; reliable quality |

**My pick on your budget: Drury Inn & Suites.** The free breakfast + free evening food/drinks effectively eliminates 2 meals per day from your budget. Over 3 nights that could save you $300+.

---

### Austin (4 Nights: April 13–17)

| Hotel | Price/Night (approx.) | Pros | Cons | Why It's Good for Families |
|-------|----------------------|------|------|---------------------------|
| **Hampton Inn & Suites Austin Downtown/Convention Center** | $160–$200 | Free breakfast, pool, walkable to South Congress (10 min), Congress Ave Bridge (bats!) | Generic chain feel | Solid location, free breakfast, pool — the trifecta for family travel on a budget |
| **Hotel San José (South Congress)** | $200–$260 | Iconic SoCo location, cool courtyard pool, walkable to everything on South Congress | Small rooms, minimalist aesthetic, no breakfast | If you want the quintessential Austin vibe and the kids are easygoing; right on South Congress |
| **Drury Inn & Suites Austin North** | $140–$170 | Free breakfast + evening kickback again, pool, newer property | Not walkable to downtown (15-min drive) | If maximizing budget savings is priority; same great Drury perks but you'll need to drive everywhere |

**My pick on your budget: Hampton Inn Downtown.** Walkable location + free breakfast + pool. The location near Congress Ave Bridge is a bonus for bat-watching (see itinerary below).

---

## 3. Day-by-Day Itinerary

### SAN ANTONIO

#### April 10 (Thursday) — Arrival Day
*Goal: Easy, low-key, let kids decompress*

- **3:00–4:00 PM** — Land at SAT, pick up rental car
- **4:30 PM** — Check into hotel, let kids swim in the pool for an hour (they need to burn energy after the flight)
- **6:30 PM** — Walk the **Riverwalk** at dusk. It's magical when the lights come on. Stroll at kid-pace, let them look at the boats and bridges
- **7:15 PM** — Dinner on the Riverwalk. **Casa Rio** (the oldest restaurant on the Riverwalk — colorful, touristy, but fun for kids; Tex-Mex, outdoor tables overlooking the river). Budget ~$60 for the family
- **8:30 PM** — Walk back to hotel, crash

#### April 11 (Friday) — Full Day: The Alamo + River Boats + Market Square
*Goal: Hit the big San Antonio landmarks*

- **8:00 AM** — Breakfast at hotel (free if Drury)
- **9:00 AM** — **The Alamo** (free admission; allow 1.5 hours). The 8-year-old may fidget but the 11-year-old will likely find it cool. Grab the junior ranger-style activity guide at the entrance to keep both engaged
- **10:45 AM** — **Rio San Antonio River Cruise** ($15/adult, $7/child). 35-minute narrated boat ride along the Riverwalk. Kids love being on the water. This is the best way to see the Riverwalk
- **12:00 PM** — Lunch at **Market Square / El Mercado** (largest Mexican market in the US). Walk around the stalls, kids can pick out a small souvenir. Lunch at **Mi Tierra Café** — famous bakery/restaurant, festive decorations, great Tex-Mex. Budget ~$55
- **2:00 PM** — **San Antonio Museum of Art** or head back to the hotel for pool time (let kids choose — never underestimate the power of the pool on a trip)
- **5:00 PM** — Rest/freshen up
- **6:30 PM** — If Drury: take advantage of the free evening kickback at the hotel (free dinner essentially)
- **7:30 PM** — Evening stroll along the Riverwalk or early bedtime

#### April 12 (Saturday) — Full Day: Natural Bridge Caverns + Morgan's Wonderland
*Goal: Get outside, do something active and unique*

- **8:00 AM** — Breakfast at hotel
- **9:00 AM** — Drive 30 min north to **Natural Bridge Caverns** ($30/adult, $19/child for Discovery Tour). Stunning underground caverns — both kids will be amazed. Allow 2 hours including the tour
- **12:00 PM** — Lunch en route back (grab Whataburger — a Texas institution the kids need to experience, ~$30)
- **1:30 PM** — **Morgan's Wonderland** (if kids are active/younger-leaning) OR **DoSeum** (San Antonio's children's museum — excellent for ages 8–11, hands-on STEM exhibits, $16/person). Pick based on your kids' interests
- **4:00 PM** — Hotel pool time
- **6:00 PM** — Dinner: **Alamo Candy Company** for Texas-style candy shopping (fun stop, $10), then dinner at **Bliss** or a more casual spot. For budget: eat at the hotel kickback or grab pizza (~$40)
- **Evening** — Pack up for tomorrow's drive to Austin

#### April 13 (Sunday) — Morning in SA, Drive to Austin
*Goal: One more quick activity, then hit the road*

- **8:00 AM** — Breakfast at hotel
- **9:00 AM** — **San Antonio Missions National Historical Park** — visit **Mission San José** (the "Queen of the Missions"). Free admission, beautiful grounds, 45 minutes is enough. It's a UNESCO World Heritage Site and honestly more impressive than the Alamo
- **10:30 AM** — Check out, load the car
- **11:00 AM** — Depart for Austin

---

### AUSTIN

#### April 13 (Sunday) — Arrive in Austin
*Goal: Get settled, explore South Congress*

- **12:30 PM** — Arrive in Austin (1.5-hr drive)
- **1:00 PM** — Check in, drop bags
- **1:30 PM** — Lunch on **South Congress Avenue (SoCo)**. **Home Slice Pizza** (legendary Austin pizza, outdoor patio, kids love it, ~$40) or **Jo's Coffee** for a lighter bite and the famous "I Love You So Much" mural photo
- **3:00 PM** — Walk South Congress: browse **Big Top Candy Shop** (the kids will lose their minds), **Uncommon Objects** (weird and wonderful antique shop), **Allen's Boots** (try on cowboy boots for fun)
- **5:00 PM** — Hotel pool time
- **7:30 PM** — Walk to the **Congress Avenue Bridge** to watch **1.5 million Mexican free-tailed bats** emerge at sunset. (Peak bat season is later in summer, but by mid-April there's usually a visible colony emerging. Check with the Austin Bat Refuge for current status.) This is FREE and unforgettable
- **8:30 PM** — Dinner nearby: **Torchy's Tacos** on South Congress (~$40) — a beloved Austin chain, fun menu, kids can customize

#### April 14 (Monday) — Full Day: Barton Springs + Zilker
*Goal: Austin's outdoors*

- **8:00 AM** — Breakfast at hotel
- **9:30 AM** — **Zilker Park** and **Barton Springs Pool** ($5/adult, $3/child). A spring-fed pool that stays 68°F year-round. In April it'll feel refreshing. The 11-year-old will love it; bring towels and sunscreen. Spend the whole morning here
- **12:00 PM** — Lunch at **Zilker Park food trucks** or nearby **Barton Springs Rd** eateries (~$40)
- **1:30 PM** — **Zilker Zephyr Mini Train** (if running) or rent **kayaks/paddleboards on Lady Bird Lake** at Zilker. Family kayak rental ~$60/hr. Paddling under the bridges is a great experience
- **3:30 PM** — **Blanton Museum of Art** on UT campus (free on Thursdays, otherwise $12/adult, kids free) OR **HOPE Outdoor Gallery** (street art/graffiti park) — the kids can take cool photos
- **5:30 PM** — Rest
- **7:00 PM** — Dinner on **Rainey Street** (casual, many restaurants in converted bungalows) or hit an Austin food truck park like **The Picnic** on Barton Springs Rd. Budget ~$50

#### April 15 (Tuesday) — Full Day: Thinkery + UT Campus + Treats
*Goal: Indoor exploration + Austin culture*

- **8:00 AM** — Breakfast at hotel
- **9:30 AM** — **Thinkery** (Austin's children's museum, $14/person). Excellent for ages 8–11 — design challenges, water play, STEM exhibits. Allow 2–3 hours
- **12:30 PM** — Lunch: **Kerbey Lane Café** (Austin institution, giant pancakes, kid-friendly, ~$50)
- **2:00 PM** — Drive to **Mount Bonnell** (15 min). Climb 102 stone steps for a panoramic view of the Hill Country and Lake Austin. Free, takes 30–45 min, great photo op
- **3:30 PM** — **Amy's Ice Creams** (an Austin must, ~$20 for the family). Mexican Vanilla is the signature flavor
- **4:30 PM** — Hotel pool or free time
- **6:30 PM** — Dinner: **Austin's Pizza** or splurge at **Matt's El Rancho** (old-school Tex-Mex, beloved by locals, ~$55)
- **8:00 PM** — Walk along **Lady Bird Lake Boardwalk** (beautiful at sunset, paved trail, easy for kids)

#### April 16 (Wednesday) — Full Day: Day Trip or Hamilton Pool + Farewell Austin
*Goal: One big adventure*

**Option A: Inner Space Cavern + Round Rock Donuts (North)**
- Drive 30 min north to **Inner Space Cavern** ($26/adult, $16/child). Another great cave, different from Natural Bridge
- Stop at **Round Rock Donuts** on the way back (Texas-famous, orange-glazed donuts, ~$15)

**Option B: Hamilton Pool Preserve (West — requires reservation)**
- **Hamilton Pool Preserve** — a stunning collapsed grotto with a 50-ft waterfall. Reservation required (book at reserves.traviscountytx.gov the moment they open). $12/vehicle. 45-min drive from Austin. One of the most beautiful natural spots in Texas. Note: swimming may or may not be open in April depending on water quality testing, but the hike and views are worth it regardless
- Pack a picnic lunch

**Either way, back by mid-afternoon:**
- **3:00 PM** — Final South Congress shopping/souvenir run
- **5:00 PM** — Pack and prep for tomorrow
- **7:00 PM** — Farewell dinner: **Franklin Barbecue** is legendary but the line is insane (2–3 hours). Instead, go to **la Barbecue** or **Terry Black's BBQ** (much shorter waits, still world-class Texas BBQ). The kids MUST try brisket before leaving Texas. Budget ~$65

#### April 17 (Thursday) — Drive to Houston
*Goal: Get to Houston, easy evening*

- **8:00 AM** — Breakfast at hotel
- **9:00 AM** — Check out
- **9:15 AM** — Depart for Houston (~2.5 hours to Hobby Airport area via TX-71 → I-10, or SH-130 → I-10)
- **11:45 AM** — Arrive Houston. Options:
  - If flying April 18 morning: check into a **hotel near Hobby Airport** (La Quinta, Holiday Inn Express — ~$100–$120). Drop bags, then explore
  - **Space Center Houston** ($30/adult, $25/child) — THE must-do in Houston with kids. Allow 3–4 hours. See real rockets, touch a moon rock, tram tour to NASA facilities. The 11-year-old especially will remember this forever
- **5:00 PM** — Return rental car at HOU Hobby (or keep overnight and return morning of April 18; check if the extra day cost is worth the convenience)
- **6:30 PM** — Dinner near hotel (~$50)
- Early bedtime for morning flight

#### April 18 (Friday) — Fly Home
- Return rental car at HOU if not done previous evening
- Flight home to Seattle

---

## 4. Top 5 Kid-Friendly Activities

### San Antonio
1. **Rio San Antonio River Cruise** — Narrated boat ride on the Riverwalk. Fun, easy, scenic
2. **Natural Bridge Caverns** — Underground adventure, genuinely awe-inspiring
3. **The Alamo** — Historic and free; short enough to hold attention
4. **The DoSeum** — Hands-on children's museum, STEM-focused, excellent for 8–11
5. **Market Square (El Mercado)** — Colorful shopping, great food, cultural immersion

### Austin
1. **Barton Springs Pool** — Iconic spring-fed swimming hole, unforgettable
2. **Congress Avenue Bridge Bats** — Watching 1.5 million bats emerge at sunset (free!)
3. **Thinkery** — Top-tier children's museum
4. **Lady Bird Lake Kayaking** — Paddling through downtown Austin
5. **Mount Bonnell** — Easy climb with a huge payoff view

**Bonus Houston stop:** Space Center Houston — arguably the single best kid activity on the entire trip

---

## 5. Driving Routes

### San Antonio → Austin
- **Route:** I-35 North — straightforward, no alternate needed
- **Distance:** 80 miles
- **Time:** 1 hour 20 min (without stops)
- **Worthwhile stop:** **New Braunfels** (halfway point) — cute German-Texas town. Stop at **Buc-ee's** (the world's most famous gas station/convenience store — enormous, spotlessly clean, with walls of snacks, fudge, jerky, and beaver nuggets). Kids will think it's an amusement park. Allow 20–30 minutes
- **Alternative:** If you want to avoid I-35 traffic, take **SH-130** (toll road, ~$5) — faster, less congested, but no interesting stops

### Austin → Houston (Hobby Airport)
- **Route:** US-290 East → I-610 South → HOU Hobby — OR — SH-130 South to I-10 East → I-610
- **Distance:** ~165 miles
- **Time:** 2.5–3 hours depending on Houston traffic
- **Tips:** Leave by 9 AM to arrive before Houston lunch traffic. Avoid arriving 4–6 PM (Houston rush hour is brutal)
- **Fuel:** Fill up leaving Austin. There are gas stations along US-290 but spacing is wider in the rural stretch. One fill-up midway in **Brenham** (home of Blue Bell Ice Cream — the factory tour may be available, check ahead)
- **Gas cost estimate:** ~$60–$75 total for the whole trip (Texas gas is cheap, ~$2.80–$3.20/gal)

---

## 6. Budget Breakdown

| Category | Estimated Cost |
|----------|---------------|
| Rental car (8 days, mid-size SUV, one-way SAT→HOU) | $420 |
| San Antonio hotel — Drury Inn (3 nights × $180) | $540 |
| Austin hotel — Hampton Inn Downtown (4 nights × $180) | $720 |
| Houston hotel — airport area (1 night) | $110 |
| Activities (caverns, river cruise, DoSeum, Thinkery, Barton Springs, kayaks, Space Center Houston) | $400 |
| Food/dining (8 days × ~$80/day, offset by free breakfasts/Drury kickbacks) | $450 |
| Gas (~500 miles total) | $65 |
| Miscellaneous (souvenirs, parking, tolls, snacks) | $100 |
| **Total** | **$2,805** |

### Budget Notes
- **You're close to $3,000** with ~$200 buffer. This assumes free breakfasts and using the Drury evening kickback for 3 dinners
- **If over budget, cut:** Space Center Houston ($110 for 4), kayaking ($60), or one restaurant meal. Swap for free activities (Lady Bird Lake hike, Zilker Park, Mount Bonnell, bat bridge)
- **If under budget:** Splurge on Terry Black's BBQ or Hamilton Pool day trip
- **Hotel prices are the biggest variable.** Book early — Spring Break week pushes Austin hotel rates up significantly. If the Hampton Inn is over $200/night, look at the Drury Austin North ($140–$170) and accept the drive

---

## 7. Practical Tips

### Best Apps
- **Roadtrippers** — Maps your route with attractions, food stops, and quirky roadside spots along the way
- **GasBuddy** — Find cheapest gas (useful in Texas)
- **Beli** — Restaurant recommendations (better than Yelp for food-focused searching)
- **AllTrails** — If you do any hiking (Mount Bonnell, Hamilton Pool)
- Kids' entertainment: download **Spotify playlists** and **audiobooks** (Audible) before leaving. The drives are short but an audiobook makes them feel instant

### What to Pack in the Car
- **Swimsuits and towels** (Barton Springs, hotel pools — you'll swim almost every day)
- Refillable water bottles (Texas in April = 75–85°F)
- Sunscreen and hats
- A small cooler for road snacks and drinks (saves money vs. gas station stops)
- Phone chargers and a car USB splitter
- One change of clothes in the car (not buried in the trunk) — kids spill things
- Light jackets for evenings (April nights can drop to low 60s)

### April Events to Know About
- **Fiesta San Antonio** — This is HUGE. Fiesta typically runs mid-to-late April. If your dates overlap (check fiesta-sa.org), you'll encounter parades, food festivals, and a LOT of crowds. It's fun but makes hotel prices spike and the Riverwalk gets packed. In 2025, Fiesta runs **April 10–20** — **you're right in it!** This is actually great: free parades, Fiesta food (chicken on a stick!), incredible energy. Just be prepared for crowds and book hotels NOW
- **Bats:** The Congress Avenue bat colony typically returns by mid-March, so by April 13 you should see bats. Emergence is usually around 7:45–8:15 PM in April
- **Bluebonnets:** Texas bluebonnets (the state flower) peak in **early-to-mid April**. You will see them along I-35 and rural roads. Stop for photos — it's a Texas tradition. The stretch between San Antonio and Austin on I-35 often has great patches

---

**Book now:** Hotels (Fiesta week will sell out), rental car (lock in a rate), and Hamilton Pool reservation (if you want it for April 16). Everything else can be decided on the go. Have an amazing trip! 🤠
